step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Inventory: the whiteboard shows a hospital/client icon, a pathologist icon, EKS, two separate S3 buckets (left = raw images, right = trained models), SageMaker, FSx and IAM. The two S3 icons play distinct roles, so they are kept as separate nodes. 2) Flow 0 (ingestion and labeling): hospitals, biologists and clients send medical images to the raw S3 bucket (about 5 TB per project); the data is loaded into the product on Kubernetes (EKS), shown to pathologists, who annotate and label it. 3) Flow 1 (training): the enriched data is used to train one model per project in SageMaker, using the same Docker containers as before, with FSx for IO performance and IAM for security; the model is stored in the second S3 bucket. 4) Flow 2 (validation and inference): model and results are exported from the model bucket to the EKS product and shown to the pathologist, who validates or rejects; once validated the model is frozen and served for inference on the same Kubernetes platform, used by the hospital. No edge was drawn for hospital inference use, so it is recorded only in notes. 5) Edge types: data for payloads, control for IAM access control, meta for the pathologist's validation feedback.

graph.name: Kinai - Medical Image Labeling and Per-Project Model Training on EKS and SageMaker
graph.notes: Healthcare company building technology for research and clinical studies, guiding pathologists and doctors in analyzing medical images. Benefits versus the previous static infrastructure: scientists work on several projects at once and switch project in seconds, thousands of trainings in parallel, training more than 30 times faster, infrastructure cost reduced by up to 30% (pay only when resources are used). Compliance: HDS certification, data kept in the project's region (e.g. a German project keeps data in Germany).

nodes.name: Hospitals / Biologists / Clients
nodes.notes: Hospitals, biologists and clients send medical images. Also the end users of the validated model for inference.

nodes.name: Pathologist
nodes.notes: Enriches the data by annotating and labeling images; reviews model results and validates or rejects the model.

nodes.name: S3 Raw Images Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores incoming medical images; about 5 TB of data per project. Data stays in the project's region.

nodes.name: EKS Product Platform
nodes.notes: Product on Kubernetes: labeling platform for pathologists, displays model results, and serves inference once the model is validated and frozen.

nodes.name: SageMaker Training
nodes.notes: Trains one model per project using the same Docker containers as the previous pipelines (easy migration). Thousands of parallel trainings, more than 30x faster, up to 30% infrastructure cost savings.

nodes.name: FSx
nodes.notes: Used with SageMaker training for IO performance.

nodes.name: IAM
nodes.notes: Security and fine-grained control of data access; supports documenting and complying with certifications such as HDS.

nodes.name: S3 Model Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores the trained model and results.
